disposition_reason: Primary ICP-OES analysis of 16 elements in 13 retail canned, jarred and frozen vegetables (wet weight).

study.design: Retail survey of 13 canned, jarred and frozen vegetable products
study.market: local supermarkets, Balikesir, Turkiye (randomly chosen brands)
study.method: Microwave HNO3 digestion (CEM Mars 5) of about 1.0 g homogenized sample; ICP-OES; three independent digestions per sample
study.qa: NIST SRM 1549a whole milk powder: recoveries 93.6-107.8% for Ba, Ca, Fe, Cu, Mg, Zn (no CRM values for Pb or Cd); blanks

findings.notes: Mean ± SD of three independent digestions of one retail product. Text gives 1.34 ± 0.10 mg/kg. Only Pb result above LOD; high for peas, single product.

controls.control: Packaging/processing: frozen vs canned (tin can) for the same vegetable
controls.comparator: canned product of the same vegetable
controls.outcome: Green peas Pb 1.3 (frozen) vs nd (<0.11 mg/kg, canned); green beans Ni 0.204 (frozen) vs nd (canned); single products of different brands, so packaging effect is confounded

unresolved: Cd LOD 52.41 ug/kg and Pb LOD 109.65 ug/kg are high relative to typical vegetable levels, so non-detects do not show low contamination.
CRM recoveries were reported only for Ba, Ca, Fe, Cu, Mg and Zn; accuracy for Pb and Cd is not demonstrated.
Pb in frozen green peas printed as 1.3 ± 0.1 (Table 3) and 1.34 ± 0.10 mg/kg (text).
